thesis: NVDA closed 225.16 on 8/14, consolidating in a 216-227 range beneath its 120-day high of 236.54, with SMA20 210.40 and SMA50 206.52 both rising underneath it. The mechanism is pre-earnings drift into the 8/26 print, but only from a better cost basis: at 225 the reward-to-risk to the 236.54 range high is 1.3, which fails the 2.0 swing minimum, so this is a wait-for-pullback limit order rather than a buy here.

catalyst.event: FOMC minutes from the July 28-29 meeting, released 14:00 ET; the curve reaction is the trade
catalyst.action: build the position before the release; add on a dovish steepening reaction, cut on a hawkish flattening

thesis: The 10y-2y spread widened to +0.51 on 8/14 from +0.48, with the 2y at 4.15% against a 3.63% effective funds rate — a bull steepener, which mechanically widens regional-bank net interest margin because these banks fund short and lend long. KRE closed 77.93, only 0.54% below its 120-day high of 78.35, with SMA20 76.48 and SMA50 74.81 stacked rising beneath it, so the balance-sheet story and the tape agree.
key_risk: A hawkish set of minutes on 8/19 that re-prices the front end higher would flatten the curve and hit KRE directly — this is the same catalyst that makes the trade, running in reverse.
counter_argument: One day of spread widening (0.48 to 0.51) is inside the noise band for the 10y-2y, and KRE is buying at the top of a 120-day range rather than at support. If the steepener is a head-fake, the entry is close to the worst price in three months.

thesis: TGT is the single large US retailer trading at its highs into this earnings week: it closed 154.48, just 1.27% under its 120-day high, while HD sits 14.07% off its high, LOW 22.30%, WMT 14.71% and TJX 10.52% off theirs. Its SMA20 of 145.85 is well above its SMA50 of 137.71, so TGT has been re-rating for months while the peer group de-rated, and that dispersion — not the sector — is the thesis.
key_risk: This is a binary event held through the print. ATR14 is 3.92 and retail earnings gaps routinely exceed 2 ATR, so the 142 stop can be gapped through at the 8/19 open with no chance to exit at it.
counter_argument: Buying a retailer at a 120-day high immediately before it reports is paying full price for a coin flip. The bear reading of the same dispersion is that TGT simply has the most embedded expectation of any retailer in the group, which is exactly what makes a miss expensive.

catalyst.event: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report, 10:30 ET Wednesday
catalyst.action: enter on a pullback into the zone before Wednesday; size small and treat any ceasefire headline as an immediate exit regardless of level

thesis: Energy was the strongest sector into the weekend — XLE +1.39% and USO +1.26% on 8/14 — and it rallied the day AFTER Brent and WTI each fell more than 2% on 8/13 to $87.07 and $81.25, which means equity buyers stepped in against a lower crude tape. XLE closed 61.91 with SMA20 59.16 above SMA50 56.97 and price 2.44% under its 120-day high of 63.46, so the trend structure is intact and the entry is a pullback rather than a chase.
key_risk: The oil bid rests on the ongoing US-Iran war supply premium. A ceasefire or de-escalation headline arrives without warning and on a weekend, and would gap crude and XLE down through the 57.80 stop before it can be worked.
counter_argument: Crude fell 2% on 8/13 specifically on falling demand, not supply — if the demand signal is the real one, the war premium is the only thing holding energy up, and premiums decay. A sector where the bull case is that a war continues is a sector with a short and unpleasant tail.

catalyst.event: FOMC minutes 14:00 ET — the liquidity/rates read that is the most likely trigger to break a 0.53%/day volatility compression
catalyst.action: DO NOT BUY AT SPOT 62,959. Rest a bid only into the 58,200-60,000 flush zone at the 120-day low; if BTC instead reclaims and closes above SMA20 63,838 first, this setup is void and the momentum entry is a different trade

thesis: BTC closed 62,958.81, below its SMA20 63,837.75, SMA50 63,514.36 and SMA100 66,876.46, and it is printing the exact low of its own 14-day range — the weakest point of the recent structure. Its average absolute daily move over 14 days is $332.70, or 0.53%, which is extreme volatility compression for this asset and historically resolves in an expansion; the value of this idea is that the 120-day low at 58,566 gives a real level to define risk against, which is not true anywhere in the current range.
key_risk: Every moving average is above price and sloping down, so this is a countertrend buy into a downtrend. Volatility compression is directionless — it can resolve straight through 58,566 and the 55,500 stop just as easily as it bounces.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that there is no crypto-specific dated catalyst at all here — the FOMC minutes are a borrowed catalyst, and borrowing an equity-macro event to justify a crypto entry is how a bad trade gets a respectable-looking reason attached to it. A trader with no edge in crypto this week should simply skip the asset class.

thesis: GLD and SLV both bottomed on the same session, 2026-07-16, at 364.96 and 50.39 — a joint capitulation low across two separately-traded metals is far harder to dismiss as single-instrument flow than either chart alone. GLD has since recovered to 401.48 and now sits above a rising SMA20 of 383.06 and SMA50 of 381.30, so the entry leans on a month-old confirmed low with a defined failure point rather than on a guess about where a decline stops.
key_risk: This is a countertrend recovery inside a larger downtrend: GLD is still 19% below its 2026-01-29 peak of 495.90, and the 423-427 shelf that sets the first target is exactly where the January and May supply sits.
counter_argument: The strongest case against is that this is a bear-market rally in an asset that has fallen for six straight months, and that I am reading a joint bottom into what is simply two correlated metals doing the same correlated thing. It also shares its rate-path direction with the KRE, IWM and BTC ideas — a hawkish 8/19 hurts all of them together, so it is a hedge against equity risk-off but NOT against the rate-path bet this book is already making.

thesis: WATCHLIST at conviction 2 on catalyst grounds, not on setup grounds. IBB has the cleanest trend structure I found after KRE and GLD: it closed 198.26, just 1.72% below its 120-day high of 201.72, with SMA20 192.00 stacked above SMA50 186.28 and both rising, and an ATR14 of only 1.79% which would allow an unusually tight stop for the target distance.
key_risk: Biotech is long-duration and rate-sensitive, so a hawkish 8/19 FOMC minutes would hit it through the same channel as the rest of this book — it is less of a diversifier than the sector label suggests.

Publishing this would mean dressing a chart up as an event, which is the exact failure mode the catalyst rule exists to prevent.
